display.title: Episode 360: The Return of Yehudah, Chapter 5 (Shabbos Shira and Tu B'Shvat)
display.summary_short: Uncle Yossi announces the Jewish Children's Expo, a young yeshiva boy leads the Shema, and Reb Moshe and Sarah must go on without little Yehudah. Plus tidying your room, and Tu B'Shvat.
display.summary_long: Broadcast in the week of Shabbos Shira and Tu B'Shvat 5749. Uncle Yossi opens with big news: Tzivos Hashem's Jewish Children's Expo returns to the Javits Center in New York in early Adar, with hours for schools and for the public. After the Hakochainik march, a six-and-a-half-year-old boy from the Lubavitcher Yeshiva leads the Shema in Studio 604. Story time continues The Return of Yehudah: Reb Moshe and Sarah, unable to go back to the pit for little Yehudah without being caught by the cruel poritz, say Tehillim, put their trust in Hashem with Rabbi Akiva's words 'all that Hashem does is for the good', and settle in a village where Reb Moshe becomes the melamed, never forgetting their son. A boy's letter from Monsey and his homemade Shiviti sign lead to a Shiviti sign contest. The morning-routine lesson continues: after negel vasser, make your bed and tidy your room to help Mommy. The show ends with candle-lighting time, Shabbos Shira, and the meaning of Tu B'Shvat: a person is like a tree, and our fruits are Torah and mitzvos.
display.lesson: Trust Hashem even when you cannot understand what is happening, and help at home by keeping your own room neat.

date.note: Consistent with the audio: candle lighting Friday January 20; 'this Shabbos is Shabbos Shira' and Tu B'Shvat.

advisories.note: Parents who escaped a cruel poritz cannot go back for their young son left behind in a pit.
A cruel poritz would put the escaped Jewish family to death if they returned.

privacy.note: Shema guest and a letter writer named in full on air.

sources_cited.note: Rabbi Akiva: 'All that the Merciful One does is for the good.'
'A person is like a tree of the field', as explained by the Sages.
